## Academic projects

- [INFO 200 Transfer Evaluation System](https://info200.joechamdani.cloud/): Student-facing tool predicting credit transfers to UW from transcripts, intended majors, and historical data, generating advisor requests and downloadable reports. Code: https://github.com/JosephDavisC/INFO-200-Final-Project
- [INFO 201 AI Job Market and LLM Growth](https://uw.joechamdani.com/projects/INFO_201/final_report_group_2): Analysis in R of how large language model expansion from 2018 to 2024 relates to AI job demand and salaries, using Kaggle datasets. Code: https://github.com/JosephDavisC/INFO_201_Final_Project
- [INFO 300 Human Judgment vs. AI Alerts](https://uw.joechamdani.com/projects/INFO_300/): Research proposal on how users interpret and trust scam detection alerts from automated systems versus humans, examining accuracy, reliability, and decision-making behavior.
- [INFO 340 Planathon](https://planathon.web.app/): Hackathon organizer web app consolidating task management, milestone tracking, team coordination, and event info. Code: https://github.com/JosephDavisC/INFO_340
- [INFO 360 UW Nap Spot Finder](https://info360.joechamdani.com/): High-fidelity interactive prototype for finding quiet nap spots across UW campus, with an interactive map, real-time availability, noise filters, walking directions, and check-in. Code: https://github.com/JosephDavisC/INFO_360
- [INFO 380 Course Registration System](https://info380.joechamdani.com): Registration prototype with student, advisor, and admin workflows, real-time search, conflict detection, waitlist management, and enrollment analytics. Code: https://github.com/JosephDavisC/INFO_380
- [INFO 498 Resonance Game Concept](https://joechamdani.com/archive/info498resonance/): Team game concept from UX Design for Games, a third person action adventure rooted in Greek mythology, taken from pitch and mood boards through an interactive character selection prototype.
- [INFO 498 Witcher 3 UX Makeover](https://joechamdani.com/archive/info498/): Interactive redesign of The Witcher 3 inventory system, rebuilding the shop, repair, and inventory flows around search, sorting, and clearer item comparison.

## Research interests

Where AI systems meet the people who have to trust them.

- AI security and red teaming: finding where language models fail, and building tooling that surfaces those failures automatically.
- Applied AI in education, especially systems that make institutional processes like credit transfer legible to the students they affect.
- Human AI interaction: how people read, trust, and override automated decisions, and what an interface owes them when a model is uncertain.
- Building AI products end to end, from problem framing through evaluation to the parts that break in production.
- Reliability of systems people depend on, including monitoring, failure modes, and the distance between something working and something being watched.

The INFO 300 proposal is the clearest example of this in his coursework: it studies how people trust AI scam alerts compared to human ones.
